business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Srivasavi Adhesive Tapes Limited manufactures, coats, converts and die-cuts industrial specialty self-adhesive tapes made from film, foam, foil, fabric and paper, along with customised die-cuts of films, foams and allied products. Products are largely made to customer specification and application, and are supplied to industries including automotive, locomotives, aerospace, defence, electrical and electronics, renewable energy, print and paper, food and pharma, FMCG, white and brown goods, furniture, retail, construction, infrastructure, sports and fitness equipment and textiles and leather. The company operates 300+ SKUs across eight product lines under its 'Dollar' brand, with a domestic presence in 21+ states and exports to 27+ countries, and is adding a Polymer Division making its own pressure-sensitive adhesives and sealants.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Industrial specialty self-adhesive tapes:** Filament tapes, Fiber glass fabric tapes, Polyester tapes, Cotton fabric tapes, Double sided tapes, Scrim tapes, Reinforced foil tape, Reinforced paper tape, High temperature resistant polyester tapes, Aluminum foil tapes, ECO friendly paper tapes, BOPP Packaging tapes, Protection tapes, Surface Protection tapes, Masking tapes, Foams Tapes, Specialty Foams/ Films

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Largest growth drivers are stated to be India's fastest-growing industrial sectors: Railways & Infrastructure (benefiting from India's capital expenditure cycle), Lithium-ion Batteries (India's expanding EV manufacturing ecosystem), Renewable Energy (clean energy transition) and Home Appliances (resilient domestic demand)
- India's specialty adhesive tape market remains over 65% import-dependent, primarily on imports from Korea and Japan - management frames this as a significant structural opportunity
- Tariff reductions in the United States are expected to further improve competitiveness in global industrial markets
- Qualifications with major EMS manufacturers continue to progress; once validated, the sector has the potential to deliver significant volume growth and margin expansion
- Defence relationships require time to develop but offer exceptional margin stability and recurring revenue opportunities
- Backward integration into in-house adhesives is expected to protect margins and build a sustainable, high-margin competitive advantage in import substitution
- The Polymer Division's 6,000 tonnes per annum capacity will support both captive consumption and new product opportunities in adjacent sectors
- Management expects the FY 2025-26 capacity-building investments (new facilities, people, approvals, entry into new sectors) to translate into durable, recurring business and stronger, more profitable growth in the years ahead
- MD&A: the outlook for the overall industries is described as positive, with growth in the Indian economy and demand creating opportunities to invest in core businesses; several developmental activities have been planned for the next fiscal year
- MD&A threats: price is the deciding factor in most cases and competition comes from both organised and unorganised players, some with greater resources
- Six Non-Disclosure Agreements signed with prospective customers across strategic industry segments - two in the Lithium-ion Battery sector, one in Electronics Manufacturing Services, one in Automotive and two with leading retail brands - described as strengthening the pipeline in high-growth markets
- A five-year purchase agreement of the Polymer Division with a leading multinational company, effective 1st July 2026, to supply PP, HDPE and technical woven fabric products, with indicative annual volumes expected to increase during the initial years, providing long-term business visibility
- Some innovations have already achieved 95% qualification for EMS applications; qualifications with major EMS manufacturers continue to progress

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Backward/vertical integration: build Unit 5 at Dabaspet as a Polymer Division making the company's own pressure-sensitive adhesives and sealants, to support import substitution and protect margins
- Capacity expansion: scale the manufacturing footprint from 2 lakh to over 4 lakh square feet
- Sector diversification: expand into Defence, EMS, Railways and other high-growth industrial sectors
- Export expansion: raise international presence from the current 15% of revenue
- Enter the Electronics Manufacturing Services ecosystem, particularly battery pack manufacturers in the electric-vehicle segment, as India's EMS market localises
- Upgrade Unit 1 into a modern Label Division with purpose-built infrastructure to widen the product portfolio
- Strengthen R&D and New Product Development to meet demanding industry specifications and move into high-value applications
- Plan Unit 6 with solar power infrastructure to optimise the cost structure
- Deliberately pursue a high-barrier path - institutional relationships, product specifications and certifications - rather than maximising short-term profit in commodity segments
- Maintain a diversified multi-unit manufacturing structure (specialty adhesive tapes, adhesives, polymer products, woven fabrics, diecuts and labels) to reduce business concentration risk
- MD&A outlook: improve market position by focusing on technologically advanced and more profitable product and market segments, and work aggressively on productivity, efficiency and cost reduction
- Increase reach by expanding the client base across sectors and verticals

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY 2025-26 is described by the Managing Director as a transformational year driven by substantial investments: fixed assets increased from Rs 15 crore to Rs 23 crore during the year, with an additional Rs 11 crore invested in Capital Work-in-Progress. Three initiatives anchor the expansion. Unit 5 at Dabaspet, the company's pioneering Polymer Division, is targeted to commence operations by Q2 of FY 2026-27 with a capacity of 6,000 tonnes per annum; it is a vertical/backward integration initiative to manufacture the company's own pressure-sensitive adhesives and sealants for import substitution, supporting both captive consumption and new product opportunities in adjacent sectors. Unit 1 was transformed during the year into a modern Label Division with purpose-built infrastructure and advanced manufacturing capabilities for high-quality labels. Unit 6 is 'on the horizon', planned and designed with solar power infrastructure to optimise the cost structure. Under its four strategic pillars the company intends to scale its manufacturing footprint from 2 lakh to over 4 lakh square feet, diversify into Defence, EMS and Railways, and expand exports from the current 15% of revenue, towards a stated ambition of a Rs 1,000 crore enterprise. The Polymer Division has also entered a five-year purchase agreement with a leading multinational company effective 1st July 2026 to supply PP, HDPE and technical woven fabric products. The named capital-commitments disclosure states there were no capital commitments outstanding at the reporting date.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Part-I Approval from Indian Railways for auto-adhesive tapes - a certification management says takes years to earn and is extremely difficult to replicate, validating quality for institutional buyers
- Backward integration into in-house pressure-sensitive adhesives and sealants, described as developing the foundational chemistry rather than only converting tapes, supporting import substitution and margin protection
- Wide, customer-specification-driven product range (300+ SKUs across eight product lines) that lets the company serve diverse customer segments and reduces business concentration risk
- Diversified multi-unit manufacturing ecosystem, each unit with a distinct purpose and dedicated product portfolio (specialty adhesive tapes, adhesives, polymer products, woven fabrics, diecuts and labels), creating operational synergies
- R&D and New Product Development capability, with some innovations already at 95% qualification for EMS applications
- ISO 9001:2015 certification by TUV Nord and multi-level in-process quality checks
- Established distribution reach - 21+ states domestically and exports to 27+ countries, including PSA shipments to South Korea
